t: Entity Attribute Extractor: a plain-language overview
title: Entity Attribute Extractor: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Entity Attribute Extractor does and why archives need it. An entity attribute extractor reads text about a person, place, or thing and writes down its facts: name, dates, location, occupation, and more. It turns a paragraph like 'Marie Curie, born in Warsaw in 1867, was a physicist' into a neat row of labeled properties. Prose goes in, structured facts come out.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Entity Attribute Extractor works
title: How the Entity Attribute Extractor works
description: Overview: what the Entity Attribute Extractor does and why archives need it. Real extractors start with named entity recognition (NER) — statistical or neural models like spaCy's pipelines label persons, organizations, locations, and dates — then fill attribute slots with patterns: 'born in X', 'founded in YEAR', dependency paths linking entities to their modifiers. Infobox-style structured blocks are parsed directly when present. Each attribute gets a value, a source span, and a confidence score, and coreference resolution ('she', 'the company') links pronouns back to their entities before extraction.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Entity Attribute Extractor works: the deep tour
title: How the Entity Attribute Extractor works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Entity Attribute Extractor does and why archives need it. Real extractors start with named entity recognition (NER) — statistical or neural models like spaCy's pipelines label persons, organizations, locations, and dates — then fill attribute slots with patterns: 'born in X', 'founded in YEAR', dependency paths linking entities to their modifiers. Infobox-style structured blocks are parsed directly when present. Each attribute gets a value, a source span, and a confidence score, and coreference resolution ('she', 'the company') links pronouns back to their entities before extraction. Advanced systems use relation-aware extraction where attributes are typed (dates must parse, populations must be numbers), validate values against expected ranges, and merge attributes across documents with conflict resolution. Quality is measured by slot-level precision and recall on annotated corpora. The limits are implied attributes ('the young prodigy' implies an age range, not a fact), sarcasm, and fictional texts — extracted attributes from those are flagged by source genre rather than presented as real-world truth.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.
